memory_update.text: Add AMKR as a direct US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging candidate for the AI accelerator/HBM/2.5D packaging node; monitor advanced packaging utilization and Arizona capacity ramp evidence.
Add ONTO as an inspection/metrology candidate tied to HBM and chiplet packaging yield; strongest evidence needed is production-scale HBM/advanced-packaging orders and backlog durability.
Add FORM as an HBM wafer-probe card candidate; customer qualification with all three major HBM manufacturers is a key Serenity-style stickiness signal.
Add TER as an AI compute and HBM/DRAM test-equipment candidate; the research question is whether test intensity and HBM share gains create a structural rather than cyclical revenue driver.
Add ENTG as an adjacent materials/contamination-control candidate for advanced nodes and advanced packaging; relevance is indirect but qualification barriers may be high.

This pass did not include non-US-primary Asian suppliers such as SK hynix, Samsung, ASE, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, or Disco, even though they may be closer to physical bottlenecks in HBM, substrates, dicing/grinding, and packaging.
Potential US-listed follow-up candidates for a later pass include CAMT, KLIC, MKSI, KLAC, AMAT, LRCX, COHU, and ICHR, but they require tighter evidence mapping to this specific node before inclusion.

node: AI accelerators, HBM, advanced-node foundry, and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI accelerator/HBM/advanced-packaging node toward second-order suppliers that can benefit if bottlenecks migrate from front-end wafers and accelerator design into OSAT capacity, wafer probing, final test, metrology/inspection, and high-purity materials. The five candidates are not buy/sell recommendations; they are research candidates where the Serenity question is whether customer qualification, process complexity, or booked capacity creates harder-to-replace exposure than the market currently recognizes.
